text:
Recommendation: Keep the 25% stake, but put it on a 4-year vesting schedule with a 1-year cliff, ideally applied to both founders' shares.
Why:
- Vesting is standard template language, not extra complexity; the costly, difficult part is unwinding a fully-vested grant later.
- Without vesting, if he leaves early he keeps the full 25% permanently, and reversing that requires his consent.
- Investors commonly flag unvested founder equity as a red flag during due diligence.
Risks and unknowns:
- No cash or outside investment exists yet to help size the risk objectively.
- He may interpret a vesting cliff as a sign of distrust; applying the same vesting terms to your own shares can help address this.
- The period before any investor is involved is when this risk is highest.
Next steps:
1. Before Monday, confirm nothing has been signed yet, and get a vesting template or lawyer involved for both of you.
2. Offer equal vesting terms and title to both founders; success means both sign within week 1, stop if he rejects vesting entirely.
3. If incorporated in the US, file the 83(b) election within 30 days of the grant.
Note: If he is contributing IP or cash on day one, that portion could reasonably vest immediately rather than over time.
